title: Your First R Program
subtopics: Saving and Running an R Script
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of your first r program and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply executing an expression in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Your First R Program is one step in Introduction to R; start with base R and short expressions. Separate displayed output from values returned by expressions. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: Executing an Expression
items.text: Explain executing an expression in the context of your first r program, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: Printing Text and Results

items.title: Saving and Running an R Script
items.text: Explain saving and running an r script in the context of your first r program, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: Understanding Output and Errors
items.text: For understanding output and errors, include a failing or boundary case and explain how it should be detected without silently losing information.

items.title: Building a Small First Program
items.text: Build the smallest example for building a small first program, inspect the returned object, and confirm its names, type and shape before using it downstream.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Begin with console work; then move the same tested expressions into a saved script. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Your First R Program
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 8: Your First R Program
example_value <- 3
example_value + 1
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: Run the expression in a local R console and confirm the returned value. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For your first r program, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

content.task: Apply your first r program to a small synthetic example. Start with executing an expression, predict the result, compare it with a local R run, test one edge or failure case, and document one limitation. For integrations or package-dependent topics, submit a safe verification plan rather than claiming the code ran.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the executing an expression idea in a minimal example or safe design sketch.
State the expected result before running the example.
Verify one relevant boundary, missing-value or failure case.
Record assumptions and one limitation of the result.

hints: Start with “Executing an Expression” and identify the input and output before coding.
Inspect the type and shape of the result, then test one ordinary and one boundary input.
Test a boundary, missing, invalid or failure input relevant to this topic.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
